about.name: Gold as a Safe Haven Strategy

hasPart.name: What makes gold unique as a safe haven asset?
hasPart.text: What makes gold unique as a safe haven asset?

acceptedAnswer.text: No counterparty risk - it doesn't depend on anyone's promise to pay

comment.text: Gold is unique because it has no counterparty risk - unlike bonds or bank deposits, it doesn't depend on anyone's promise to pay and simply exists, retaining value independent of any institution's solvency.

hasPart.name: During the 2008 financial crisis, how did gold perform while stocks fell 57%?
hasPart.text: During the 2008 financial crisis, how did gold perform while stocks fell 57%?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gold rose from around $800 to over $1,900 (137% gain)

comment.text: During the 2008 financial crisis, while the S&P 500 fell 57%, gold rose from around $800 to over $1,900 in the following years, representing a 137% gain and demonstrating its safe haven properties.

suggestedAnswer.text: Gold fell by the same amount

hasPart.name: What was gold's extraordinary performance during the 1970s stagflation period?
hasPart.text: What was gold's extraordinary performance during the 1970s stagflation period?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gold rose 2,200% from $35 to $800 per ounce

comment.text: During the 1970s stagflation period, gold rose an extraordinary 2,200% from $35 to $800 per ounce, demonstrating its ability to protect wealth during periods of high inflation and economic stagnation.

hasPart.name: What is the recommended core safe haven allocation for conservative investors?
hasPart.text: What is the recommended core safe haven allocation for conservative investors?

comment.text: Conservative investors with low risk tolerance are recommended to maintain a 10-15% precious metals allocation for capital preservation and stability during market downturns.

hasPart.name: During the COVID-19 pandemic, what happened to gold prices?
hasPart.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, what happened to gold prices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gold reached new all-time highs above $2,000 per ounce

comment.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, while stocks crashed 35% in weeks, gold reached new all-time highs above $2,000 per ounce, with continued strength through 2024 reaching over $3,300.

hasPart.name: What are early warning indicators that suggest increasing safe haven allocation?
hasPart.text: What are early warning indicators that suggest increasing safe haven allocation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yield curve inversion and credit market stress

comment.text: Early warning indicators include yield curve inversion (which often precedes recessions), credit market stress with rising corporate bond spreads, and central bank policy shifts.

hasPart.name: Why is physical gold preferred over paper gold for true safe haven protection?
hasPart.text: Why is physical gold preferred over paper gold for true safe haven protection?

acceptedAnswer.text: No counterparty risk and available even if financial systems fail

comment.text: Physical gold is preferred for safe haven protection because it has no counterparty risk and remains accessible even if financial systems fail, unlike ETFs or certificates that depend on financial institutions.

suggestedAnswer.text: Physical gold is easier to trade

hasPart.name: True or False: Central banks have been significant gold buyers, purchasing over 1,000 tonnes per year since 2010.
hasPart.text: True or False: Central banks have been significant gold buyers, purchasing over 1,000 tonnes per year since 2010.

comment.text: True. Central banks worldwide have become significant gold buyers, purchasing over 1,000 tonnes per year since 2010 as they diversify reserves and prepare for potential financial system stress.

hasPart.name: What is a common mistake in safe haven strategy implementation?
hasPart.text: What is a common mistake in safe haven strategy implementation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waiting for crisis to buy safe haven assets

comment.text: A common mistake is waiting for crisis to buy safe haven assets. Safe haven assets should be purchased before you need them, during calm periods, not during the crisis itself when prices may be elevated.

suggestedAnswer.text: Using physical gold instead of ETFs
